t2i_prompt: A 1440 px wide desktop website section as a flat straight-on UI mockup: a deep navy blueprint panel on a warm limestone page. A small mono uppercase eyebrow over a hairline rule, then a large light-weight sans headline with a steel-blue mono uppercase aside on its baseline. A row of five pale blue-white hairline line icons sits above a continuous steel-blue double-line pipe crossing the panel, with P&ID valve symbols and tiny mono tags between them. Below, five columns: large light numeral, mono uppercase title and short sans text for <CONTENT>. Flat, square corners, calm.
signature_idea: The five steps hang off one steel-blue double-line pipe, with a P&ID valve between each step as the gate to the next.
strengths: pipe-as-timeline is a strong, on-offer metaphor and buildable in SVG
light numerals, mono titles and steel-blue accent are the brand pairing
placeholders in brackets follow the site rule
weaknesses: icons are generic and uneven in detail (busy cabinet vs simple document)
valve tags are repeated filler codes (AQ-421 twice)
rounded panel corners and bottom glow break the square, flat rules
mono aside 'stages of progression' is filler copy
valves sit between steps, not aligned to them
brand_fit_why: Navy, limestone, one steel-blue accent, light headline and mono labels fit closely; rounded corners, glow and filler tags cost a point.
